[VPlan] Use llvm.mask.beforefirst for computing early exit mask (#212717)

This makes the cost more accurate on AArch64 and improves codegen for
RISC-V and X86. The codegen for an early exit loop with side effects on
RISC-V goes from:

```asm
    .LBB0_3:                                # %vector.body
                                            # =>This Inner Loop Header: Depth=1
    	vl1r.v	v16, (a3)
    	vsetvli	zero, zero, e8, m1, ta, ma
    	vmseq.vi	v16, v16, 0
    	vfirst.m	a7, v16
    	srli	t0, a7, 63
    	czero.nez	a7, a7, t0
    	czero.eqz	t0, a1, t0
    	or	a7, t0, a7
    	vsetvli	zero, zero, e64, m8, ta, ma
    	vmsltu.vx	v0, v8, a7
    	vle8.v	v17, (a5), v0.t
    	vcpop.m	t1, v16
    	vsetvli	zero, zero, e8, m1, ta, ma
    	vadd.vi	v16, v17, 1
    	vse8.v	v16, (a5), v0.t
    	sub	a4, a4, a2
    	bnez	t1, .LBB0_5
```

To

```asm
    .LBB0_3:                                # %vector.body
                                            # =>This Inner Loop Header: Depth=1
    	vl1r.v	v8, (a4)
    	vmseq.vi	v8, v8, 0
    	vmsbf.m	v0, v8
    	vle8.v	v9, (a5), v0.t
    	vcpop.m	t0, v8
    	vadd.vi	v9, v9, 1
    	vse8.v	v9, (a5), v0.t
    	sub	a2, a2, a3
    	bnez	t0, .LBB0_5
```

[MLIR] Make tblgen broadcast emission order compiler independent (#3786)

enzyme-tblgen emitted gutils->broadcastToWidth(...) calls inline in the
argument list of the Op::create(...) call. The evaluation order of
function arguments is unspecified in C++, so the order of the created
enzyme.broadcast ops depended on the host compiler (GCC evaluates
right-to-left, Clang left-to-right), making ReverseMode/arith.mlir fail
when built with Clang.

Emit each broadcast as its own statement ahead of the create call, in
operand order, and update the test expectations accordingly.

commit.message:
[TPDE,X64] Don't use a temporary register for extensions

Extensions from >32 bits where src and dst reg are identical are rare
enough, so avoid allocating a separate register and use a slightly less
efficient instruction sequence (1->2 uops, 13->8 bytes).

This fixes a bug when generating calls, which assumes that
generate_raw_intext doesn't allocate registers.

cranelift-frontend: fix i128 Switch jump table indexing above 2^63 (#15293)

To compute the jump table index (val - first_index) for a contiguous
range of cases, Switch::build_jump_table previously emitted
`iadd_imm_s(val, (first_index as i64).wrapping_neg())` whenever
first_index fit in u64.

For i128, iadd_imm_s sign-extends its 64-bit immediate to 128 bits.
When first_index is in `(1 << 63, u64::MAX]`, negating it as an i64
produces a positive value, so sign-extension pads the upper 64 bits
with zeros instead of ones (off by 2^64). The resulting index then
failed the u32::MAX bounds check and every case in the range fell
through to the default block.

This commit materializes `first_index` via `iconst_from_u128` and
subtracts it directly with `isub`.

Reboot TypeGeneralizing to use ChildTyper (#9359)

This works out nicely actually, using the optional binary-format type
hints in the ChildTyper API to send the generalized types that we infer.

This is a good starting point for productionizing the pass.

[IRBuilder] Hoist input gets across none exprs (#9338)

Input scratch locals are never modified while their initial `local.get`
expressions remain on the expression stack, so `hoistLastValue` can move
them directly across subsequent `none`-typed expressions without
allocating a new scratch local or creating a synthetic block. Track
whether a local is an input local of the current scope via
`ScopeCtx::isInputLocal` and use the same check when tunneling inputs in
`pushScope`.

Note that optimizing input parameters in `IRBuilder` cannot disturb
tests that expect the parsed IR to closely mirror the input WAT, because
Binaryen IR does not have control flow input parameters and such tests
therefore do not use them.

String returns for small strings, JSON::stringify and Intl; Date::new_with_value; ArrayBuffer bytes (#5446)

* String returns for small strings, JSON::stringify and Intl; Date::new_with_value; ArrayBuffer bytes

Under js_sys_unstable_apis, built-in members whose result is a small
string return String rather than JsString, as Symbol::to_string already
did, so callers no longer write `String::from(err.message())`:
Error::message/name/to_string, the Date string formatters,
Number::to_fixed/to_precision/to_exponential/to_string_with_radix,
RegExp::source/flags/to_string, Function::name, and the string fields of
the Intl resolved options and format parts. JSON::stringify and
stringify_with_replacer return Result<Option<String>, JsValue>, None for a
value with no JSON form (undefined, a function, a symbol), and the
replacer's key is a String.

Also under the cfg: Date::new_with_value takes a time value or a date
string (impl JsNumberOrStringLike), and ArrayBuffer converts to and from
bytes (to_vec, From<&[u8]>, From<Vec<u8>>, and Vec<u8>: From<ArrayBuffer>
and From<&ArrayBuffer>).

Tests that read these results work under both cfgs, and wasm-export-colon
is re-blessed for the cfg-hashed Error::message/name shim names.

* Date::to_json is Option<String>, ArrayBuffer::to_vec handles detached buffers, SegmentData::input stays JsString

`Date.prototype.toJSON` returns `null` for an invalid date, which threw
in the glue when read as `String`, so the unstable `to_json` returns
`Option<String>`. `new Uint8Array` throws on a detached buffer, so
`ArrayBuffer::to_vec` and the `Vec<u8>` conversions return an empty `Vec`
when `byteLength` is 0. `SegmentData::input` is the whole segmented text,
so it stays a `JsString`. The CHANGELOG and guide now list
`Symbol::to_string` and the `Intl` `format` / `format_range` changes.

* From<JsValue> for Error and its subclasses wraps a non-error value

A caught exception or a promise rejection can be any JS value and reaches
an error type through From<JsValue>, which was an unchecked cast, so
Error::message and Error::name, now String, threw in the glue on a value
with no string message. Under js_sys_unstable_apis the conversion wraps a
value without a string message and name in a new error of that type, with
the value as its cause.

The new no_from_js_value attribute omits the generated From<JsValue> impl
for an imported type so that the error types can provide their own.

* Keep the generated casts and ABI glue of an imported type unchecked

The generated unchecked_from_js, from_abi, ref_from_abi and
long_ref_from_abi built the inner handle through From<JsValue> of the
first extends type, so a subclass of Error ran its wrapping conversion in
unchecked_into and in the glue, and on a borrowed argument dropped the
borrowed handle. They now use unchecked_into.

Update ACP SDK to 5.3.0 and follow schema 1.18 rule changes (#66979)

Updates `agent-client-protocol` to 5.3.0 (schema 1.18.0) and brings what
Zed already implements in line with the rules that changed.

- **Plan operations: the `file` plan type is removed.** Markdown plans
carry an optional absolute `path` instead, and the client always renders
`content`. A markdown plan with a `path` keeps the collapsible plan row
and gets an "Open Plan File" button. A relative `path` is ignored, so
the plan has no file. Naming or changing the file counts as a change to
the plan, so it re-shows a dismissed plan, as a new URI did for file
plans.
- **Unknown v2 command types are no longer offered as slash commands.**
The spec used to let a client show a command type it doesn't understand
as a plain command. It now says the client must not. The composer only
offers `command` entries for completion, input hints, validation, and
the "/ for commands" placeholder. `AcpThread` still keeps the full list.
This also covers the new `skill` entries, which Zed doesn't advertise
support for.
- **The new `speed` config option category converts from v1.** The
`unstable` SDK feature now parses `speed` as a known category. The v1
conversion rejected categories it didn't list, so one `speed` option
would have failed the agent's whole option list.

Checked against the 1.18 docs, no change needed:

- `replay_complete` (v2) is ignored. Zed still treats the
`session/resume` response as the end of replay and discards the thread
when a resume fails, and the RFD keeps the subagent freshness boundary
at the response.
- The subagent clarifications already hold. An `unknown` state shows as
unconfirmed, and a session message without a sender renders as a message
from another session.
- Zed doesn't send `tool_call/cancel` or `terminal/cancel` once the tool
call is final or the terminal has exited.
- Zed doesn't call `session/options` or `session/fork`, so the new rules
for them don't apply.

Not adopted yet: prompt suggestions, Agent Skills, placing `speed`
options next to the model selector, and using `replay_complete` to show
replayed history before the resume response.

commit.message:
windows: direct Win32 calls go through bun_sys (#49166)

### What does this PR do?

Code above `bun_sys` called Win32 directly, often through an `extern`
block of its own. It now uses safe wrappers in `bun_sys::windows`, and
the raw functions are no longer re-exported from there.

- A ConPTY handle is a `PseudoConsole`, which can only be closed once.
- `SetEndOfFile`, `FlushFileBuffers`, `GetCurrentThread` and
`TerminateProcess` take no pointer and are declared `safe`.
- `bun_spawn_sys` no longer depends on `bun_windows_sys`.

No change in behavior is intended.

The completion port calls of the watcher and the vectored exception
handler are left for later.

### How did you verify your code works?

The new wrappers, compiled on their own, pass 28 checks under Wine. Wine
has no `ResizePseudoConsole`. I have not run Bun itself on Windows, so
the callers are only type-checked locally and rely on CI.

`rust:check-all`, clippy for Linux and the source lints pass, and so do
the terminal, spawn, os and crash handler tests on a Linux x64 debug
build.
